data.body:
CLOSED as duplicate — no gate change and no --force were needed.

The gate was NOT defective. close_precheck already has exactly this disposition path:
_NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES = {duplicate, not_a_bug, escalated}, and when the close class
is one of those AND _has_live_replacement_link() finds a live replacement, the precheck
routes to close_disposition.verdict() instead of demanding fix evidence.

The blocker was DATA, not policy: this ticket named 6a81 / 0d78 / b0f5 only in DESCRIPTION
PROSE, and _has_live_replacement_link reads reduced-state 'deps' for a 'duplicates'
relation. deps was []. So the precheck fell through to the ordinary completion verifier,
which synthesized 'Bug <title> is actually resolved' from the title and correctly failed
it — the defect genuinely is not resolved here; it is carried by 6a81.

Fix: rebar link 9b70 6a81 duplicates. The close then passed on the next attempt.

WORTH FIXING SEPARATELY (discoverability): the failure message sent the reader the wrong
way. It offered only 'complete the work' or '[operator-attested]' — attesting would have
been a FALSE claim of resolution — and never mentioned that a non-completion --class needs
a replacement LINK. When close_class is in _NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES but no live
replacement link exists, the error should say so and name the 'link <id> <canonical>
duplicates' remedy. That is the difference between a two-minute fix and the long detour
this took.
